title: Pierce NiNTA Magnetic Beads Part 2
author: Opentrons
materials: Step 4-6 repeats 1 more time, if desired.

steps.title: Move plate to magnetic module
steps.instruction: Place the 96‑well deep‑well working plate containing the bead‑protein mixture onto the magnetic module in slot 1 to start Part 2.

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: With the magnetic module engaged, use the 8‑channel pipette to aspirate and discard the supernatant from each well.

steps.title: First wash of beads
steps.instruction: Wash the bead‑protein complex with wash buffer and remove the wash supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Transfer wash buffer (50 mM sodium phosphate, 300 mM NaCl, 40 mM imidazole, pH 7.4) from slot 4 to the working plate in slot 1 using the 8‑channel pipette.
Turn the magnetic module off and resuspend the precipitated beads by mixing.
Turn the magnetic module back on to re‑precipitate the beads.
Aspirate and discard the wash supernatant with the 8‑channel pipette (reuse the same tips).

steps.title: Second wash (optional)
steps.instruction: Repeat the first wash step using the same tips if a second wash is desired.

steps.title: First elution buffer addition
steps.instruction: Add elution buffer and resuspend the beads to begin protein elution.

substeps.instruction: Transfer elution buffer (50 mM sodium phosphate, 300 mM NaCl, 300 mM imidazole, pH 7.4) from slot 2 to the working plate (slot 1) with the 8‑channel pipette.
Turn the magnetic module off and resuspend the beads thoroughly.

steps.title: Incubate with agitation
steps.instruction: Seal the plate, shake for 10 minutes at room temperature, then return it to the magnetic module.

substeps.instruction: Place the sealed plate on a shaker and agitate for 10 min at room temperature.
Move the plate back to the magnetic module in slot 1.

steps.title: Collect eluate
steps.instruction: With the magnetic module engaged, use the 8‑channel pipette to transfer the eluate to the final plate in slot 2.

steps.title: Second elution (optional)
steps.instruction: If increased recovery is desired, repeat steps 5‑7 a second time.
